key_insight: High PVS segmentation accuracy did not guarantee valid Alzheimer’s biomarker associations; only AD-trained models reproduced the expected PVS–amyloid relationship.
clinical_relevance: Automated PVS measurements may support Alzheimer’s research, but require cohort-specific validation before clinical inference.
method: Benchmarked five open-source nnU-Net-based models against manual PVS labels.
Evaluated segmentation across regions, diagnoses, scanners, PVS severity, and white matter hyperintensity burden.
Tested whether model-derived PVS burden preserved manual-label associations with AD biomarkers.
evidence_signal: Testing included 60 multi-site ADNI-3 participants and 12 external VALDO scans; ADNI-PVS-Net achieved internal Dice of 0.58 ± 0.14 but external Dice ≤0.11.
watch_item: External testing was limited to 12 scans, and some models misclassified up to 32% of white matter hyperintensities as PVS.
paper_title: Examining the Clinical Utility of Deep Learning Models for Perivascular Space Segmentation in Alzheimer's Disease
